meaning: Two Purushas there are in this world: the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are perishable, and the Kutastha—the unchanging—is called the imperishable.

transliteration:
uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ
paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ |
yo lokatrayamāviśya
bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ ||17||
meaning: But distinct is the Supreme Purusha, called the highest Self, indestructible and Lord, who pervades the three worlds and sustains them.

transliteration:
yasmātkṣaramatīto'ham
akṣarādapi cottamaḥ |
ato'smi loke vede ca
prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ||18||
meaning: As I transcend the perishable and am even higher than the imperishable, I am declared to be the highest Purusha in the world and in the Vedas.

transliteration:
yo māmevamasammūḍhaḥ
jānāti puruṣottamam |
sa sarvavid bhajati māṁ
sarvabhāvena bhārata ||19||
meaning: He who, undeluded, knows Me as the highest Purusha, he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being (heart), O Arjuna.

transliteration:
iti guhyatamaṁ śāstram
idamuktaṁ mayā'nagha |
etadbuddhvā buddhimānsyāt
kṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata ||20||
meaning: Thus, I have imparted to you this most secret science, O sinless one; by knowing this, one becomes wise, and all their duties are accomplished, O Arjuna.

speaker: śrī bhagavān uvāca
transliteration:
abhayaṁ sattvasaṁśuddhiḥ
jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ |
dānaṁ damaśca yajñaśca
svādhyāyastapa ārjavam ||1||
meaning: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, almsgiving, control of the senses, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, and straightforwardness.

transliteration:
ahiṁsā satyamakrodhaḥ
tyāgaḥ śāntirapaiśunam |
dayā bhūteṣvaloluptvaṁ
mārdavaṁ hrīracāpalam ||2||
meaning: Harmlessness, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion for beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and absence of fickleness.

transliteration:
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucam
adroho nātimānitā |
bhavanti sampadaṁ daivīm
abhijātasya bhārata ||3||
meaning: Vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of hatred, absence of pride—these belong to one born for a divine state, O Arjuna.

transliteration:
dambho darpo'bhimānaśca
krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca |
ajñānaṁ cābhijātasya
pārtha sampadamāsurīm ||4||
meaning: Hypocrisy, arrogance, and self-conceit, anger, harshness, and ignorance—these belong to one who is born for a demoniacal state, O Partha.

transliteration:
daivī sampadvimokṣāya
nibandhāyāsurī matā |
mā śucaḥ sampadaṁ daivīm
abhijāto'si pāṇḍava ||5||
meaning: The divine nature is deemed conducive to liberation, and the demonic to bondage. Grieve not, O Arjuna, for you are born with divine endowments.

transliteration:
dvau bhūtasargau loke'smin
daiva āsura eva ca |
daivo vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ
āsuraṁ pārtha me śṛṇu ||6||
meaning: There are two types of beings in this world: the divine and the demoniacal. The divine has been described at length; hear from Me, O Arjuna, about the demoniacal.

transliteration:
pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca
janā na vidurāsurāḥ |
na śaucaṁ nāpi cācāraḥ
na satyaṁ teṣu vidyate ||7||
meaning: The demoniacal do not know what to do and what to refrain from; they have neither purity, nor right conduct, nor truth.

transliteration:
asatyamapratiṣṭhaṁ te
jagadāhuranīśvaram |
aparasparasambhūtaṁ
kimanyatkāmahaitukam ||8||
meaning: They say, "This universe is without truth, without a moral basis, without a God, brought about by mutual union, with lust as its cause; what else?"

transliteration:
etāṁ dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya
naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ |
prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ
kṣayāya jagato'hitāḥ ||9||
meaning: Holding this view, these ruined souls of small intellect and fierce deeds come forth as enemies of the world, intent on its destruction.

transliteration:
kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṁ
dambhamānamadānvitāḥ |
mohādgṛhītvā'sadgrāhān
pravartante'śucivratāḥ ||10||
meaning: Filled with insatiable desires, full of hypocrisy, pride, and arrogance, holding evil ideas due to delusion, they work with impure intentions.

transliteration:
cintāmaparimeyāṁ ca
pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ |
kāmopabhogaparamāḥ
etāvaditi niścitāḥ ||11||
meaning: Giving themselves over to immeasurable cares that end only with death, regarding the gratification of lust as their highest aim, and feeling sure that that is all.

transliteration:
āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ
kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ |
īhante kāmabhogārtham
anyāyenārthasañcayān ||12||
meaning: Bound by a hundred ties of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain hoards of wealth by unlawful means for sensual enjoyment.

transliteration:
idamadya mayā labdham
imaṁ prāpsye manoratham |
idamastīdamapi me
bhaviṣyati punardhanam ||13||
meaning: "I have gained this today; I will fulfill this desire of mine; this is mine, and this wealth will be mine in the future."

transliteration:
asau mayā hataḥ śatruḥ
haniṣye cāparānapi |
īśvaro'hamahaṁ bhogī
siddho'haṁ balavānsukhī ||14||
meaning: "I have slain that enemy, and I shall slay others too. I am the Lord; I enjoy, I am perfect, powerful, and happy."

transliteration:
āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi
ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā |
yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣye
ityajñānavimohitāḥ ||15||
meaning: "I am wealthy and born into a noble family. Who is my equal? I shall perform sacrifices, give charity, and rejoice," thus deluded by ignorance.

transliteration:
anekacittavibhrāntāḥ
mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ |
prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu
patanti narake'śucau ||16||
meaning: Bewildered by many fancies, entangled in the snare of delusion, addicted to the gratification of lust, they fall into a foul hell.

transliteration:
ātmasambhāvitāḥ stabdhāḥ
dhanamānamadānvitāḥ |
yajante nāmayajñaiste
dambhenāvidhipūrvakam ||17||
meaning: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only for ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances.

transliteration:
ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ
kāmaṁ krodhaṁ ca saṁśritāḥ |
māmātmaparadeheṣu
pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ ||18||
meaning: Given over to egoism, power, haughtiness, lust, and anger, these malicious people hate Me in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.

transliteration:
tānahaṁ dviṣataḥ krūrān
saṁsāreṣu narādhamān |
kṣipāmyajasramaśubhān
āsurīṣveva yoniṣu ||19||
meaning: Those cruel haters, the worst among men in the world, I hurl those evil-doers into the wombs of demons only.

transliteration:
āsurīṁ yonimāpannāḥ
mūḍhā janmani janmani |
māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya
tato yāntyadhamāṁ gatim ||20||
meaning: Entering into demoniacal wombs and deluded, birth after birth, they do not attain Me, thus falling, O Arjuna, into a condition still lower than that.

transliteration:
trividhaṁ narakasyedaṁ
dvāraṁ nāśanamātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhaḥ
tasmādetattrayaṁ tyajet ||21||
meaning: There are three gates to this hell, destructive of the self: lust, anger, and greed; therefore, one should abandon these three.

transliteration:
etairvimuktaḥ kaunteya
tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ |
ācaratyātmanaḥ śreyaḥ
tato yāti parāṁ gatim ||22||
meaning: A person who is liberated from these three gates of darkness, O Arjuna, practices what is beneficial for them and thus goes to the Supreme Goal.

transliteration:
yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya
vartate kāmakārataḥ |
na sa siddhimavāpnoti
na sukhaṁ na parāṁ gatim ||23||
meaning: He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the scriptures, acts under the impulse of desire, does not attain perfection, nor happiness, nor the Supreme Goal.

transliteration:
tasmācchāstraṁ pramāṇaṁ te
kāryākāryavyavasthitau |
jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṁ
karma kartumihārhasi ||24||
meaning: Therefore, let the scripture be thy authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known what is said in the ordinance of the scriptures, thou shouldst act in this world.

speaker: arjuna uvāca
transliteration:
ye śāstravidhimutsṛjya
yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ |
teṣāṁ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa
sattvamāho rajastamaḥ ||1||
meaning: Arjuna said, "What is the condition of those who, disregarding the injunctions of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith—is it Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas, O Krishna?"

speaker: śrī bhagavān uvāca
transliteration:
trividhā bhavati śraddhā
dehināṁ sā svabhāvajā |
sāttvikī rājasī caiva
tāmasī ceti tāṁ śṛṇu ||2||
meaning: The Blessed Lord said, "There are threefold faiths inherent in the nature of the embodied: the sattvic (pure), the rajasic (passionate), and the tamasic (dark). Hear of them."

transliteration:
sattvānurūpā sarvasya
śraddhā bhavati bhārata |
śraddhāmayo'yaṁ puruṣaḥ
yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ ||3||
meaning: The faith of each is in accordance with their nature, O Arjuna. People consist of their faith; as a person's faith is, so are they.

transliteration:
yajante sāttvikā devān
yakṣarakṣāṁsi rājasāḥ |
pretān bhūtagaṇāṁścānye
yajante tāmasā janāḥ ||4||
meaning: The sattvic, or pure, men worship the gods; the rajasic, or passionate, worship the yakshas and rakshasas; the others, the tamasic or deluded people, worship ghosts and hosts of nature-spirits.

transliteration:
aśāstravihitaṁ ghoraṁ
tapyante ye tapo janāḥ |
dambhāhaṅkārasaṁyuktāḥ
kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ ||5||
meaning: Those men who practice terrific austerities not prescribed by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, driven by the force of lust and attachment.

transliteration:
karśayantaḥ śarīrasthaṁ
bhūtagrāmamacetasaḥ |
māṁ caivāntaḥ śarīrasthaṁ
tān viddhyāsuraniścayān ||6||
meaning: Know thou these to be of demonical resolves, senselessly torturing all the elements in the body and Me who dwell in the body.

transliteration:
āhārastvapi sarvasya
trividho bhavati priyaḥ |
yajñastapastathā dānaṁ
teṣāṁ bhedamimaṁ śṛṇu ||7||
meaning: The food that is dear to each is threefold, as well as sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Hear the distinction of these.

transliteration:
āyussattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ |
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyāḥ
āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ ||8||
meaning: The foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, joy, and cheerfulness (good appetite), which are savory, oily, substantial, and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic (pure) people.

transliteration:
kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ |
āhārā rājasasyeṣṭāḥ
duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ ||9||
meaning: The foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief, and disease.

transliteration:
yātayāmaṁ gatarasaṁ
pūti paryuṣitaṁ ca yat |
ucchiṣṭamapi cāmedhyaṁ
bhojanaṁ tāmasapriyam ||10||
meaning: That which is stale, tasteless, putrid, rotten, rejected, and impure is the food liked by the Tamasic.

transliteration:
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryajñaḥ
vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate |
yaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ
samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ ||11||
meaning: That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for reward, as enjoined by the ordinance (scripture), with a firm faith that doing so is their duty, is Sattvic or pure.

transliteration:
abhisandhāya tu phalaṁ
dambhārthamapi caiva yat |
ijyate bharataśreṣṭha
taṁ yajñaṁ viddhi rājasam ||12||
meaning: The sacrifice that is offered, O Arjuna, seeking a reward and for show, know that to be a Rajasic Yajna.

transliteration:
vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṁ
mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam |
śraddhāvirahitaṁ yajñaṁ
tāmasaṁ paricakṣate ||13||
meaning: They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, and which is devoid of mantras, gifts, and faith.

transliteration:
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṁ śaucamārjavam |
brahmacaryamahiṁsā ca
śārīraṁ tapa ucyate ||14||
meaning: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers, and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy, and non-injury are all called the austerities of the body.

transliteration:
anudvegakaraṁ vākyaṁ
satyaṁ priyahitaṁ ca yat |
svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ caiva
vāṅmayaṁ tapa ucyate ||15||
meaning: Speech that causes no excitement, is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial; the practice of studying the Vedas is called austerity of speech.

transliteration:
manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṁ
maunamātmavinigrahaḥ |
bhāvasaṁśuddhirityetat
tapo mānasamucyate ||16||
meaning: Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, self-control, and purity of nature—this is called mental austerity.

transliteration:
śraddhayā parayā taptaṁ
tapastat trividhaṁ naraiḥ |
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ
sāttvikaṁ paricakṣate ||17||
meaning: This threefold austerity, practiced by steadfast men, with the utmost faith, desiring no reward, is called Sattvic.

transliteration:
satkāramānapūjārthaṁ
tapo dambhena caiva yat |
kriyate tadiha proktaṁ
rājasaṁ calamadhruvam ||18||
meaning: The austerity that is practiced with the aim of gaining good reception, honor, and worship, and with hypocrisy, is said to be Rajasic, unstable, and transient.

transliteration:
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yat
pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
parasyotsādanārthaṁ vā
tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||19||
meaning: That austerity which is practised out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be of the Tamasic nature.

transliteration:
dātavyamiti yaddānaṁ
dīyate'nupakāriṇe |
deśe kāle ca pātre ca
taddānaṁ sāttvikaṁ smṛtam ||20||
meaning: That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a suitable place and time to a worthy person, is held to be Sattvic.

transliteration:
yattu pratyupakārārthaṁ
phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ |
dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṁ
taddānaṁ rājasaṁ smṛtam ||21||
meaning: And, that gift which is given with the intention of receiving something in return, or expecting a reward, or begrudgingly, is considered to be Rajasic.

transliteration:
adeśakāle yaddānam
apātrebhyaśca dīyate |
asatkṛtamavajñātaṁ
tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||22||
meaning: The gift that is given in the wrong place and at the wrong time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult, is declared to be of a Tamasic nature.

transliteration:
om tatsaditi nirdeśaḥ
brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
brāhmaṇāstena vedāśca
yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā ||23||
meaning: "Om Tat Sat": This has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that, the Brahmanas, the Vedas, and the sacrifices were created formerly.

transliteration:
tasmād om ityudāhṛtya
yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ |
pravartante vidhānoktāḥ
satataṁ brahmavādinām ||24||
meaning: Therefore, with the utterance of "Om," the acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity, as enjoined in the scriptures, are always begun by the students of Brahman.

transliteration:
tadityanabhisandhāya
phalaṁ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ |
dānakriyāśca vividhāḥ
kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ ||25||
meaning: Uttering "Tat," without aiming for the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice, austerity, and the various acts of gifts performed by those seeking liberation.

transliteration:
sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca
sadityetat prayujyate |
praśaste karmaṇi tathā
sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate ||26||
meaning: The word "Sat" is used to refer to reality and goodness; likewise, O Arjuna, the word "Sat" is used to refer to an auspicious act.

transliteration:
yajñe tapasi dāne ca
sthitiḥ saditi cocyate |
karma caiva tadarthīyaṁ
sadityevābhidhīyate ||27||
meaning: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and gift is also called 'Sat', and action in connection with these, or for the sake of the Supreme, is also called 'Sat'.

transliteration:
aśraddhayā hutaṁ dattaṁ
tapastaptaṁ kṛtaṁ ca yat |
asadityucyate pārtha
na ca tatpretya no iha ||28||
meaning: Whatever is sacrificed, given, or performed, and whatever austerity is practiced without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Arjuna; it is of no value here or hereafter (after death).

transliteration:
||oṁ tatsaditi śrīmanmahābhārate
śatasāhasrikāyāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ
śrīmadbhīṣmaparvaṇi śrīmadbhagavadgītāsu
upaniṣatsu brahmavidyāyāṁ yogaśāstre
śrīkṛṣṇārjuna saṁvāde mokṣasannyāsayogonāma
aṣṭādaśodhyāyaḥ||
Gītāmāhātmyam
Gītāmāhātmyam
dharovāca bhagavan parameśāna
bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī |
prārabdhaṁ bhujyamānasya
kathaṁ bhavati he prabho ||1||
meaning: Arjuna said, "O mighty-armed Hrishikesa, I desire to know the essence or truth of renunciation and abandonment severally, O slayer of Kesi."

transliteration:
śrīviṣṇuruvāca prārabdhaṁ bhujyamāno hi
gītābhyāsarataḥ sadā |
sa muktaḥ sa sukhī loke
karmaṇā nopalipyate ||2||
meaning: The Blessed Lord said, "The sages understand sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions to be tyaga."

transliteration:
mahāpāpādipāpāni
gītādhyānaṁ karoti cet |
kvacitsparśaṁ na kurvanti
nalinīdalamambuvat ||3||
meaning: Some philosophers declare that actions should be abandoned as evil; while others declare that acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be relinquished.

transliteration:
gītāyāḥ pustakaṁ yatra
yatra pāṭhaḥ pravartate |
tatra sarvāṇi tīrthāni
prayāgādīni tatra vai ||4||
meaning: Hear from Me the conclusion or the final truth about this abandonment, O best of the Bharatas; abandonment, indeed, O best of men, has been declared to be of three kinds.

transliteration:
sarve devāśca ṛṣayaḥ
yoginaḥ pannagāśca ye |
gopālā gopikā vā'pi
nāradoddhavapārṣadaiḥ ||5||
meaning: Acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; for sacrifice, gift, and austerity are the purifiers of the wise.

transliteration:
sahāyo jāyate śīghraṁ
yatra gītā pravartate |
yatra gītāvicāraśca
paṭhanaṁ pāṭhanaṁ śrutam |
tatrāhaṁ niścitaṁ pṛthvi
nivasāmi sadaiva hi ||6||
meaning: But even these actions should be performed, leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards, O Arjuna; this is my certain and most assured conviction.

transliteration:
gītāśraye'haṁ tiṣṭhāmi
gītā me cottamaṁ gṛham |
gītājñānamupāśritya
trīllokānpālayāmyaham ||7||
meaning: Verily, the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper; the abandonment of the same out of delusion is declared to be Tamasic.

transliteration:
gītā me paramā vidyā
brahmarūpā na saṁśayaḥ |
ardhamātrākṣarā nityā
svānirvācyapadātmikā ||8||
meaning: He who abandons action out of fear of bodily trouble (because it is painful), does not obtain the merit of renunciation by performing such Rajasic renunciation.

transliteration:
cidānandena kṛṣṇena
proktā svamukhato'rjunam |
vedatrayī parānandā
tattvārthajñānasaṁyutā ||9||
meaning: Whatever obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, merely because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and also the desire for reward, that renunciation is regarded as sattvic (pure).

transliteration:
yo'ṣṭādaśaṁ japennityaṁ
naro niścalamānasaḥ |
jñānasiddhiṁ sa labhate
tato yāti paraṁ padam ||10||
meaning: The man of renunciation, pervaded by purity, intelligent, and with his doubts cut asunder, does not hate an unpleasant task nor is he attached to a pleasant one.

transliteration:
pāṭhe'samarthaḥ sampūrṇe
tato'rdhaṁ pāṭhamācaret |
Gītāmāhātmyam
tadā godānajaṁ puṇyaṁ
labhate nātra saṁśayaḥ ||11||
meaning: Indeed, it is not possible for an embodied being to completely abandon actions; however, he who relinquishes the rewards of actions is truly called a man of renunciation.

transliteration:
tribhāgaṁ paṭhamānastu
gaṅgāsnānaphalaṁ labhet |
ṣaḍaṁśaṁ japamānastu
somayāgaphalaṁ labhet ||12||
meaning: The threefold fruit of action (evil, good, and mixed) accrues after death to those who do not abandon it, but never to those who do.

transliteration:
ekādhyāyaṁ tu yo nityaṁ
paṭhate bhaktisaṁyutaḥ |
rudralokamavāpnoti
gaṇo bhūtvā vasecciram ||13||
meaning: Learn from Me, O mighty-armed Arjuna, these five causes, as declared in the Sankhya system, for the accomplishment of all actions.

transliteration:
adhyāyaṁ ślokapādaṁ vā
nityaṁ yaḥ paṭhate naraḥ |
sa yāti naratāṁ yāvat
manvantaraṁ vasundhare ||14||
meaning: The body, the doer, the various senses, the different functions of various kinds, and the presiding deity—the fifth.

transliteration:
gītāyāḥ ślokadaśakaṁ
sapta pañca catuṣṭayam |
dvau trīnekaṁ tadardhaṁ vā
ślokānāṁ yaḥ paṭhennaraḥ ||15||
meaning: Whatever action a person performs with their body, speech, and mind, whether right or wrong, these five are its causes.

transliteration:
candralokamavāpnoti
varṣāṇāmayutaṁ dhruvam |
gītāpāṭhasamāyuktaḥ
mṛto mānuṣatāṁ vrajet ||16||
meaning: Now, such being the case, verily he who, owing to an untrained understanding, looks upon his Self, which is isolated, as the agent, he of perverted intelligence does not see.

transliteration:
gītābhyāsaṁ punaḥ kṛtvā
labhate muktimuttamām |
gītetyuccārasaṁyuktaḥ
mriyamāṇo gatiṁ labhet ||17||
meaning: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose intelligence is not tainted by good or evil, though he slays these people, he does not slay, nor is he bound by the action.

transliteration:
gītārthaśravaṇāsaktaḥ
mahāpāpayuto'pi vā |
vaikuṇṭhaṁ samavāpnoti
viṣṇunā saha modate ||18||
meaning: Knowledge, the knowable, and the knower form the threefold impulse for action; the organ, the action, and the agent form the threefold basis of action.

transliteration:
gītārthaṁ dhyāyate nityaṁ
kṛtvā karmāṇi bhūriśaḥ |
jīvanmuktaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ
dehānte paramaṁ padam ||19||
meaning: Knowledge, action, and actor are declared in the science of the Gunas (Sankhya philosophy) to be of three kinds only, according to the distinction of the Gunas. Of these, hear duly.

transliteration:
malanirmocanaṁ puṁsāṁ
jalasnānaṁ dine dine |
sakṛdgītāmbhasi snānaṁ
saṁsāramalanāśanam ||20||
meaning: That by which one sees the indestructible Reality in all beings, not separate in any of them—know that knowledge to be Sattvic.

transliteration:
gītāmāśritya bahavaḥ
bhūbhujo janakādayaḥ |
nirdhūtakalmaṣā loke
gītā yātāḥ paraṁ padam ||21||
meaning: But that knowledge which sees in all beings various entities of distinct kinds as being distinct from one another, know thou that knowledge to be Rajasic.

transliteration:
te śṛṇvanti paṭhantyeva
gītāśāstramaharniśam |
na te vai mānuṣā jñeyā
devā eva na saṁśayaḥ ||22||
meaning: But that which clings to one single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, without any foundation in Truth, and is trivial—that is declared to be Tamasic.

transliteration:
jñānājñānakṛtaṁ nityam
indriyairjanitaṁ ca yat |
Gītāmāhātmyam
tatsarvaṁ nāśamāyāti
gītāpāṭhena tat kṣaṇam ||23||
meaning: An action that is ordained, free from attachment, done without love or hatred, and without desire for reward is declared to be Sattvic.

transliteration:
dhik tasya jñānamācāraṁ
vrataṁ ceṣṭāṁ tapo yaśaḥ |
gītārthapaṭhanaṁ nā'sti
nādhamastatparo janaḥ ||24||
meaning: But that action which is done by one longing for the fulfillment of desires or gain with egotism or with much effort is declared to be Rajasic (passionate).

transliteration:
saṁsārasāgaraṁ ghoraṁ
tartumicchati yo janaḥ |
gītānāvaṁ samāruhya
pāraṁ yāti sukhena saḥ ||25||
meaning: That action which is undertaken from delusion, without regard for the consequences, loss, injury, and one's own ability, is declared to be Tamasic (dark).

transliteration:
gītāyāḥ paṭhanaṁ kṛtvā
māhātmyaṁ naiva yaḥ paṭhet |
vṛthā pāṭho bhavettasya
śrama eva hyudāhṛtaḥ ||26||
meaning: An agent who is free from attachment, non-egoistic, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is considered to be of a Sattvic (pure) nature.

transliteration:
etanmāhātmyasaṁyuktaṁ
gītābhyāsaṁ karoti yaḥ |
sa tatphalamavāpnoti
durlabhāṁ gatimāpnuyāt ||27||
meaning: Passionate, desiring to obtain the reward of their actions, greedy, cruel, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an agent is said to be Rajasic.

transliteration:
sūta uvāca māhātmyametadgītāyāḥ
mayā proktaṁ sanātanam |
gītānte ca paṭhedyastu
yaduktaṁ tatphalaṁ labhet ||28||
meaning: Unsteady, vulgar, inflexible, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—such an agent is called Tamasic.

transliteration:
buddherbhedaṁ dhṛteścaiva
guṇatastrividhaṁ śṛṇu |
procyamānamaśeṣeṇa
pṛthaktvena dhanañjaya ||29||
meaning: Hear thou the threefold division of intellect and firmness, according to the Gunas, as I declare them fully and distinctly, O Arjuna.

transliteration:
pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca
kāryākārye bhayābhaye |
bandhaṁ mokṣaṁ ca yā vetti
buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī ||30||
meaning: The intellect which knows the path of work and renunciation, what should be done and what should not be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation—that intellect is Sattvic (pure), O Arjuna.

transliteration:
yayā dharmamadharmaṁ ca
kāryaṁ cākāryameva ca |
ayathāvatprajānāti
buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī ||31||
meaning: That by which one wrongly understands dharma and adharma, and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done—that intellect, O Arjuna, is rajasic (passionate).

transliteration:
adharmaṁ dharmamiti yā
manyate tamasā''vṛtā |
sarvārthānviparītāṁśca
buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī ||32||
meaning: That intellect, O Arjuna, which is enveloped in darkness and sees Adharma as Dharma and all things perverted, is Tamasic (dark).

transliteration:
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate
manaḥ prāṇendriyakriyāḥ |
yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā
dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī ||33||
meaning: The unwavering firmness, through which Yoga restrains the functions of the mind, life-force, and senses—that firmness, O Arjuna, is Sattvic (pure).

transliteration:
yayā tu dharmakāmārthān
dhṛtyā dhārayate'rjuna |
prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī
dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī ||34||
meaning: But that, O Arjuna, by which one holds fast to Dharma (duty), enjoyment of pleasures, and earning of wealth, on account of attachment and desire for reward—that firmness, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).

transliteration:
yayā svapnaṁ bhayaṁ śokaṁ
viṣādaṁ madameva ca |
na vimuñcati durmedhāḥ
dhṛtiḥ sā tāmasī matā ||35||
meaning: That firmness, O Arjuna, by which a stupid man does not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair, and conceit, is Tamasic.

transliteration:
sukhaṁ tvidānīṁ trividhaṁ
śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha |
abhyāsādramate yatra
duḥkhāntaṁ ca nigacchati ||36||
meaning: And now, O Arjuna, hear from Me of the threefold pleasure, in which one rejoices through practice and surely comes to the end of pain.

transliteration:
yattadagre viṣamiva
pariṇāme'mṛtopamam |
tatsukhaṁ sāttvikaṁ proktam
ātmabuddhiprasādajam ||37||
meaning: That which is like poison at first but in the end like nectar—that happiness is declared to be sattvic, born of the purity of one's own mind due to self-realization.

transliteration:
viṣayendriyasaṁyogāt
yattadagre'mṛtopamam |
pariṇāme viṣamiva
tatsukhaṁ rājasaṁ smṛtam ||38||
meaning: That happiness which arises from the contact of the senses with the objects, which is initially like nectar but eventually like poison, is said to be Rajasic.

transliteration:
yadagre cānubandhe ca
sukhaṁ mohanamātmanaḥ |
nidrālasyapramādotthaṁ
tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||39||
meaning: That happiness which at first, as well as in the end, deludes the self, and which arises from sleep, indolence, and heedlessness—that is declared to be Tamasic.

transliteration:
na tadasti pṛthivyāṁ vā
divi deveṣu vā punaḥ |
sattvaṁ prakṛtijairmuktaṁ
yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ ||40||
meaning: There is no being on earth or in heaven among the gods that is liberated from the three qualities born of Nature.

transliteration:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṁ
śūdrāṇāṁ ca parantapa |
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni
svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ ||41||
meaning: Of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas, and Sudras, O Arjuna, the duties are distributed according to the qualities born of their own nature.

transliteration:
śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṁ
kṣāntirārjavameva ca |
jñānaṁ vijñānamāstikyaṁ
brahmakarma svabhāvajam ||42||
meaning: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, and uprightness, as well as knowledge, realization, and belief in God, are the duties of Brahmanas, born of their own nature.

transliteration:
śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṁ
yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam |
dānamīśvarabhāvaśca
kṣātraṁ karma svabhāvajam ||43||
meaning: Prowess, splendor, firmness, dexterity, and not fleeing from battle, generosity, and lordliness are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of their own nature.

transliteration:
kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṁ
vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam |
paricaryātmakaṁ karma
śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam ||44||
meaning: Agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade are the duties of the Vaisya (merchant), born of their own nature; and service is the duty of the Sudra (servant-class), born of their own nature.

transliteration:
sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ
saṁsiddhiṁ labhate naraḥ |
svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṁ
yathā vindati tacchṛṇu ||45||
meaning: Each person devoted to their own duty attains perfection. How they attain perfection while being engaged in their own duty, hear now.

transliteration:
yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṁ
yena sarvamidaṁ tatam |
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya
siddhiṁ vindati mānavaḥ ||46||
meaning: He from whom all the beings have evolved and by whom all this is pervaded, worshipping Him with his own duty, one attains perfection.

transliteration:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ
paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svabhāvaniyataṁ karma
kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam ||47||
meaning: Better is one's own duty, even if it is destitute of merits, than the duty of another well performed. He who does the duty ordained by his own nature incurs no sin.

transliteration:
sahajaṁ karma kaunteya
sadoṣamapi na tyajet |
sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa
dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ ||48||
meaning: One should not, O Arjuna, abandon the duty to which one is born, though it may be faulty; for, all undertakings are enveloped by evil, just as fire is by smoke.

transliteration:
asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra
jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ |
naiṣkarmyasiddhiṁ paramāṁ
sannyāsenādhigacchati ||49||
meaning: He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, from whom desire has fled, he attains the supreme state of freedom from action through renunciation.

transliteration:
siddhiṁ prāpto yathā brahma
tathā''pnoti nibodha me |
samāsenaiva kaunteya
niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā ||50||
meaning: Learn from Me, O Arjuna, in brief how one who has attained perfection reaches Brahman—the Eternal, that supreme state of knowledge.

transliteration:
buddhyā viśuddhayā yuktaḥ
dhṛtyā''tmānaṁ niyamya ca |
śabdādīnviṣayāṁstyaktvā
rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca ||51||
meaning: Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self through firmness, relinquishing sound and other objects and abandoning attraction and hatred.

transliteration:
viviktasevī laghvāśī
yatavākkāyamānasaḥ |
dhyānayogaparo nityaṁ
vairāgyaṁ samupāśritaḥ ||52||
meaning: Dwelling in solitude, eating sparingly, with speech, body, and mind subdued, always engaged in meditation and concentration, and resorting to dispassion.

transliteration:
ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ
kāmaṁ krodhaṁ parigraham |
vimucya nirmamaḥ śāntaḥ
brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||53||
meaning: Having abandoned egoism, strength, arrogance, desire, anger, and covetousness, and being free from the notion of 'mine' and peaceful, he is fit for becoming Brahman.

transliteration:
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā
na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu
madbhaktiṁ labhate parām ||54||
meaning: Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, he neither grieves nor desires; he is the same to all beings, and obtains supreme devotion to Me.

transliteration:
bhaktyā māmabhijānāti
yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ |
tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā
viśate tadanantaram ||55||
meaning: By devotion, he knows Me in truth, who and what I am; then, having known Me in truth, he immediately enters into the Supreme.

transliteration:
sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā
kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ |
matprasādādavāpnoti
śāśvataṁ padamavyayam ||56||
meaning: Having taken refuge in Me and doing all actions, by My grace he obtains the eternal, indestructible state of being.

transliteration:
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi
mayi sannyasya matparaḥ |
buddhiyogamupāśritya
maccittaḥ satataṁ bhava ||57||
meaning: Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, having Me as the highest goal, and resorting to the yoga of discrimination, do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.

transliteration:
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi
matprasādāttariṣyasi |
atha cettvamahaṅkārāt
na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi ||58||
meaning: Fixing your mind on Me, you shall, by My grace, overcome all obstacles; but if you will not hear Me due to egoism, you shall perish.

transliteration:
yadahaṅkāramāśritya
na yotsya iti manyase |
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste
prakṛtistvāṁ niyokṣyati ||59||
meaning: If, filled with egoism, thou thinkest, "I will not fight," then thy resolve is vain; nature will compel thee.

transliteration:
svabhāvajena kaunteya
nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartuṁ necchasi yanmohāt
kariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat ||60||
meaning: O Arjuna, bound by your own Karma (action) born of your own nature, that which from delusion you wish not to do, even that you shall do helplessly.

transliteration:
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ
hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni
yantrārūḍhāni māyayā ||61||
meaning: The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusory power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine.

transliteration:
tameva śaraṇaṁ gaccha
sarvabhāvena bhārata |
tatprasādātparāṁ śāntiṁ
sthānaṁ prāpsyasi śāśvatam ||62||
meaning: Fly to Him for refuge with all your being, O Arjuna; by His grace you will obtain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

transliteration:
iti te jñānamākhyātaṁ
guhyādguhyataraṁ mayā |
vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa
yathecchasi tathā kuru ||63||
meaning: Thus, wisdom more secret than secrecy itself has been declared to you by me. Reflect on it fully, then act as you wish.

transliteration:
sarvaguhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ
śṛṇu me paramaṁ vacaḥ |
iṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti
tato vakṣyāmi te hitam ||64||
meaning: Hear again My supreme word, most secret of all; for you are dearly beloved of Me, I will tell you what is good.

transliteration:
manmanā bhava madbhaktaḥ
madyājī māṁ namaskuru |
māmevaiṣyasi satyaṁ te
pratijāne priyo'si me ||65||
meaning: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. You will come to Me; I truly promise you this, for you are dear to Me.

transliteration:
sarvadharmānparityajya
māmekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja |
ahaṁ tvā sarvapāpebhyaḥ
mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||66||
meaning: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone; I will liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.

transliteration:
idaṁ te nātapaskāya
nābhaktāya kadācana |
na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṁ
na ca māṁ yo'bhyasūyati ||67||
meaning: Never speak this to one who is devoid of austerities or devotion, who does not render service, who does not desire to listen, or who cavils at Me.

transliteration:
ya imaṁ paramaṁ guhyaṁ
madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati |
bhaktiṁ mayi parāṁ kṛtvā
māmevaiṣyatyasaṁśayaḥ ||68||
meaning: He who, with supreme devotion to Me, teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, shall undoubtedly come to Me.

transliteration:
na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu
kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ |
bhavitā na ca me tasmāt
anyaḥ priyataro bhuvi ||69||
meaning: There is no one among men who does service dearer to Me, nor shall there be anyone on earth dearer to Me than him.

transliteration:
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṁ
dharmyaṁ saṁvādamāvayoḥ |
jñānayajñena tenāham
iṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ ||70||
meaning: And he who studies this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall have been worshipped through the sacrifice of wisdom; such is my conviction.

transliteration:
śraddhāvānanasūyaśca
śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ |
so'pi muktaḥ śubhāllokān
prāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām ||71||
meaning: Also, the man who hears this, full of faith and free from malice, shall attain to the happy worlds of those of righteous deeds, and be liberated.

transliteration:
kaccidetacchrutaṁ pārtha
tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā |
kaccidajñānasammohaḥ
pranaṣṭaste dhanañjaya ||72||
meaning: Has this been heard, O Arjuna, with one-pointed focus? Has the delusion of your ignorance been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?

speaker: arjuna uvāca
transliteration:
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā
tvatprasādānmayā'cyuta |
sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ
kariṣye vacanaṁ tava ||73||
meaning: Arjuna said, "My delusion has been destroyed, for I have gained my knowledge (memory) through Your grace, O Krishna. I am now free from doubts. I will act according to Your word."

speaker: sañjaya uvāca
transliteration:
ityahaṁ vāsudevasya
pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ |
saṁvādamimamaśrauṣam
adbhutaṁ romaharṣaṇam ||74||
meaning: Sanjaya said, Thus, I have heard this wonderful dialogue between Krishna and the high-souled Arjuna, which causes one's hair to stand on end.

transliteration:
vyāsaprasādācchrutavān
imaṁ guhyatamaṁ param |
yogaṁ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇāt
sākṣātkathayataḥ svayam ||75||
meaning: Through the grace of Vyasa, I have heard this supreme and most secret Yoga, directly from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, Himself declaring it.

transliteration:
rājan saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya
saṁvādamimamadbhutam |
keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṁ
hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ ||76||
meaning: O King, remembering this wonderful and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I continually rejoice.

transliteration:
tacca saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya
rūpamatyadbhutaṁ hareḥ |
vismayo me mahānrājan
hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ ||77||
meaning: And, remembering again and again that most wonderful form of Hari, I am filled with great wonder, O King; and I rejoice again and again.

transliteration:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ |
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtiḥ
dhruvā nītirmatirmama ||78||
meaning: Wherever Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, is; and wherever Arjuna, the wielder of the bow, is; there is prosperity, victory, happiness, and a firm policy; this is my conviction.
